reports.title: Ingram Micro Reports Record Q3 2026 Results, with Solid Double-Digit Growth in Net Sales and Net Income and Strong Cash Flow Generation; Raised Full Year Guidance from September Capital Markets Day

guidance.heading: Fiscal Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook
section: •Net sales for Q4 2026 expected to be $17.5 billion to $17.9 billion — a year-over-year increase of 17.6% to 20.3%
•Non-GAAP diluted EPS for Q4 2026 expected to be $1.05 to $1.15 — up from $0.96 in the prior fiscal fourth quarter

IRVINE, Calif. — (BUSINESS WIRE) — October 29, 2026 — Ingram Micro Holding Corporation (NYSE: INGM) (“Ingram Micro” or the “Company”) today reported 2026 fiscal third quarter results for the period ended September 26, 2026. The Company reported net sales of $15.2 billion, up 20.8% year-over-year, and net income on a GAAP basis of $131.1 million, or $0.57 per share, up 31.8% and 35.7% year-over-year, respectively. Non-GAAP net income of $210.6 million, or $0.91 per share,(1) was up 24.8% and 26.4% versus the same period last year, respectively.

“Our record third-quarter performance reflects the breadth and resilience of our business and continued execution against the strategy we outlined at our Capital Markets Day in September. We delivered broad-based growth across all four regions, and across our primary lines of business, while continuing to scale XvantageTM and advance our intelligent operating model," said Paul Bay, Ingram Micro’s chief executive officer. "The investments we are making in our platform, data and AI are enabling us to deepen customer engagement, improve productivity and increasingly turn intelligence into action. With our unmatched global scale, expanding platform capabilities and growing leadership in agentic commerce, we believe we are well positioned to capture the opportunities ahead and create long-term value for our shareholders.”

“Our double-digit year-over-year growth is reflective of balanced strength both geographically and by line of business, but remains most robust in Advanced Solutions, including GPU and AI infrastructure as well as Cloud-based Solutions,” said Mike Zilis, Ingram Micro’s chief financial officer. “This growth paired with disciplined expense management, drove operating income above our expectations, while disciplined working capital management contributed to our strongest third-quarter cash flow performance to date. These results demonstrate our ability to translate growth into higher earnings and cash generation while continuing to invest for sustainable, long-term shareholder returns.”
